name: Learn: Services & Networking (hardened)
objective: CKAD › Services & Networking. Drill every Service shape and the Ingress/endpoints surface: ClusterIP with named targetPort, NodePort on a pinned port, headless, ExternalName, sessionAffinity, Ingress (pathType/ingressClassName/TLS), a selector-less Service + manual EndpointSlice, and a no-hint 'no endpoints' diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.
description: Eight strict Service/Ingress practicals against a pre-seeded web Deployment. Each Check shows which requirements you met and why any failed.

questions.title: ClusterIP with a named targetPort
questions.teach:
A Service fronts label-selected pods with a stable IP/DNS. `port` is what clients hit; `targetPort` is the container port — and it can be a **named** port instead of a number (more robust). Default type is ClusterIP.

**Gotcha:** no matching *ready* pods → no endpoints.
questions.prompt:
A Deployment `web` (label `app=web`, container port **named `http`** = 80) runs in `svcnet-learn`. Create a **ClusterIP** Service `web-svc` with `port: 80` whose `targetPort` is the **named** port `http`, selecting `app=web`.

Target: `web-svc` ClusterIP, port 80 → targetPort `http`, selector app=web.
questions.hint: `targetPort: http` (the name, not 80). `kubectl -n svcnet-learn expose deployment web --name web-svc --port 80 --target-port http`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n svcnet-learn expose deployment web --name web-svc --port 80 --target-port http
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints web-svc

verification.description: web-svc ClusterIP port 80 -> targetPort 'http', selector app=web

questions.title: NodePort on a pinned port
questions.teach:
A **NodePort** opens the same port (30000–32767) on every node and forwards to the Service — it still has a ClusterIP underneath. Set `type: NodePort` and pin `nodePort`.

**Gotcha:** `nodePort` must be in 30000–32767.
questions.prompt:
Create a **NodePort** Service `web-np` for `app=web`: `port: 80`, `targetPort: 80`, pinned `nodePort: 30080`.

Target: `web-np` type NodePort, port 80 → 80, nodePort 30080, selector app=web.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn create service nodeport web-np --tcp=80:80 --node-port=30080` then set its selector to app=web (or edit), OR write YAML with `type: NodePort` and `nodePort: 30080`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: web-np, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector: { app: web }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80, nodePort: 30080 } ]
YAML

verification.description: web-np NodePort port 80 -> 80, nodePort 30080, selector app=web

questions.title: Headless Service
questions.teach:
A **headless** Service sets `clusterIP: None` — no virtual IP; DNS returns the pod IPs directly (one A record per endpoint). Used for StatefulSets / client-side load-balancing.

**Gotcha:** `clusterIP: None` is the single field that makes it headless.
questions.prompt:
Create a **headless** Service `web-hl` for `app=web` on `port: 80` (`clusterIP: None`).

Target: `web-hl` has `clusterIP: None` and selector app=web.
questions.hint: Set `clusterIP: None` in the Service spec.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: web-hl, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector: { app: web }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]
YAML

questions.title: ExternalName Service
questions.teach:
An **ExternalName** Service maps a cluster DNS name to an external one via a CNAME — no selector, no endpoints, pure DNS.

**Gotcha:** `type: ExternalName` + `externalName`; there are no ports or selector.
questions.prompt:
Create an **ExternalName** Service `db-ext` that points to `db.example.com`.

Target: `db-ext` type ExternalName, externalName `db.example.com`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn create service externalname db-ext --external-name db.example.com`.
questions.solution: kubectl -n svcnet-learn create service externalname db-ext --external-name db.example.com

questions.title: Session affinity
questions.teach:
`sessionAffinity: ClientIP` pins each client IP to the same pod (sticky sessions), tuned by `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds`.

**Gotcha:** the only options are `ClientIP` or `None`.
questions.prompt:
Create a ClusterIP Service `web-sa` for `app=web` on port 80 with **ClientIP session affinity** and a timeout of **3600** seconds.

Target: `web-sa` has `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` and `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds: 3600`.

questions.title: Ingress with pathType, class, and TLS
questions.teach:
An **Ingress** routes external HTTP(S) to Services by host/path (needs a controller to actually serve). Each path needs a `pathType`; `ingressClassName` picks the controller; `tls` terminates HTTPS with a tls Secret.

**Gotcha:** `pathType` is required on every path.
questions.prompt:
Create an Ingress `web-ing` in `svcnet-learn`:
- `ingressClassName: nginx`
- host `myapp.local`, one path `/` with `pathType: Prefix` → Service `web-svc` port `80`
- TLS for host `myapp.local` using secret `web-tls`

Target: `web-ing` has ingressClassName nginx, the Prefix `/` rule to web-svc:80, and a tls entry with secretName web-tls.
questions.hint: Set `spec.ingressClassName: nginx`, a rule with `pathType: Prefix` and `backend.service.name: web-svc` / `port.number: 80`, and `spec.tls: [{hosts: [myapp.local], secretName: web-tls}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: web-ing, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls: [ { hosts: [ myapp.local ], secretName: web-tls } ]
  rules:
  - host: myapp.local
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web-svc, port: { number: 80 } } }
YAML

verification.description: web-ing: class nginx, Prefix / -> web-svc:80, TLS secret web-tls

questions.title: Selector-less Service + manual EndpointSlice
questions.teach:
A Service with **no selector** gets no automatic endpoints — you supply them with an **EndpointSlice** labelled `kubernetes.io/service-name: <svc>`. This fronts an external/hand-managed backend.

**Gotcha:** that label is what attaches the slice to the Service.
questions.prompt:
Create a selector-less ClusterIP Service `ext-svc` (port 80), and an **EndpointSlice** attaching it to a backend at `10.40.0.9:80`.

Target: `ext-svc` has no selector, and an EndpointSlice labelled `kubernetes.io/service-name=ext-svc` with endpoint address `10.40.0.9`.
questions.hint: Service with `ports` and NO `selector`. EndpointSlice (`discovery.k8s.io/v1`) with `metadata.labels.kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc`, `addressType: IPv4`, `endpoints: [{addresses: [10.40.0.9]}]`, `ports: [{port: 80}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: ext-svc, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]
---
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: ext-svc-1
  namespace: svcnet-learn
  labels: { kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc }
addressType: IPv4
ports: [ { name: "", port: 80 } ]
endpoints: [ { addresses: [ "10.40.0.9" ] } ]
YAML

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Service with no endpoints
questions.teach:
A Service with **no endpoints** but healthy pods almost always means a **selector mismatch** (a typo or wrong label). Compare the Service's `spec.selector` to the pod labels and fix it in place.

**Gotcha:** endpoints come only from *ready* pods.
questions.prompt:
Service `api-svc` in `svcnet-learn` has **no endpoints** even though Deployment `api` (label `app=api`) is running. Diagnose and fix it so the Service has endpoints. Don't delete it.

Target: `api-svc` has at least one endpoint address.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc` (empty) then `kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` — the selector is wrong. Patch it to `app=api`: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc

verification.description: api-svc now has endpoints (selector fixed to app=api)
